newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ST COMPUTER TO REMOVE FOREIGN TRANCHE.
newsitem.headline: ST COMPUTER TO REMOVE FOREIGN TRANCHE.

text.p: ST Computer Systems & Services Ltd, a unit of Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp (STIC), said on Thursday both its local and foreign tranche shares would be traded under one category with effect on Friday August 8, 1997.
"With effect from tomorrow, both the foreign and local shares will be quoted under one tranche," a STIC spokeswoman told Reuters.
ST Computer foreign shares would no longer be quoted, she said.
The local shares of the company closed on Thursday at Singapore $1.01, down six cents. The foreign tranche closed at S$1.05, down one cent.
"Now is as good as any time," the spokeswoman said when asked about the timing of the change.
"The board of ST Computer decided the timing is good, particularly because both classes of shares are virtually trading as one due to the small price differential."
On May 2, the government-linked company won approval to raise the foreign shareholdings in the company to 49 percent from 25 percent.
The spokeswoman said STIC holds 60.8 percent of ST Computer, making a separate quotation for a foreign tranche unnecessary.

Other units within the Singapore Technologies group which still have separate local and foreign tranches are ST Electronic & Engineering , ST Aerospace, ST Shipbuilding & Engineering and ST Automotive.
The spokeswoman said all these units also obtained approval in May to raise their foreign shareholding stake to 49 percent from their existing limits.
She said it would be up to these companies individually to decide when to raise their foreign shareholding limits to 49 percent and effectively abolish their foreign tranches.
